newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable after discount rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable after discount rate cut.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in moderate early trading on Wednesday following a cut in a key discount rate, dealers said.
"The cut surprised the market but many operators had already expected the discount rate cut to take place in February or March after a cut in December," one state bank dealer said.
Bank Indonesia on Wednesday cut its key discount rates for short-term securities (SBPUs) by 50 basis points for all maturities.
Spot rupiah was generally stable and was last quoted at 2,395.75/96.25 at 0340 GMT from 2,395.80/96.80 at the opening.
One-week SBPUs fell to 14.75 percent, two to 15.0 percent, and one month to 15.50 percent.
SBPUs are papers purchased by the central bank to inject liquidity into the banking system.
The dealer said the discount rate cut had been expected following recent declines in rates of SBIs (securities issued by the central bank to absorb liquidity).
"The cut has been expected after months of generally ample rupiah liquidity and declines in SBI rates" another dealer said.
One Japanese bank dealer said the discount rate cut did not have an immediate impact on the rupiah as it was generally stable.
Dealers said the SBPU cut was seen as a signal from the central bank that interest rates were expected to be on the downward trend in the future.
Central bank director C. Harinowo told Reuters Financial Television on Wednesday that the discount rate cut decision was based on an improved outlook inflation in Indonesia.

Dealers said the rate cut, however, was not likely to push the rupiah further down, as demand for the local currency was expected to strengthen ahead of financial year reporting session in late March.
Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,395.50/96.25 and 2,395.25/95.75 respectively.
Dealers said the rupiah was expected to remain little changed on Wednesday, with spot rate seen moving in the range between 2,395.50 to 2,397.00.
Overnight swap was last quoted at 0.20/0.25 and tom/next at 0.10/0.20.
One-month swaps was last quoted at 9.50/10.25, two at 22.00/22.75, three at 35.0/36.50 and six at 74.0/74.75 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,386/2,578 and the conversion band at 2,386/2,434 late on Tuesday.
